questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Union of India' and 'Territory of India'? 1️⃣ The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India'. 2️⃣ The 'Union of India' includes only the States. 3️⃣ The 'Territory of India' includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India.
questions.e: According to Article 1, the 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India' because the latter includes only states, while the former includes not only the states, but also union territories and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any future time. States are members of the federal system and share a distribution of powers with the Centre, whereas Union Territories are directly administered by the Central government.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament's power to reorganize states under Article 3, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Parliament can form a new state by separation of territory from any state. 2️⃣ A bill for this purpose can be introduced in the Parliament only with the prior recommendation of the President. 3️⃣ The President must refer the bill to the concerned state legislature, and their views are binding on the Parliament.
questions.e: Under Article 3, Parliament is authorized to form new states or alter areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. A bill for such changes requires the prior recommendation of the President. While the President refers the bill to the concerned state legislature for its views, the Parliament is not bound by those views and may either accept or reject them.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Citizenship' provisions at the commencement of the Constitution, which of the following categories were eligible? 1️⃣ Persons domiciled in India. 2️⃣ Persons who migrated from Pakistan. 3️⃣ Persons of Indian origin residing outside India.
questions.e: The Constitution identifies four categories of persons who became citizens at its commencement on January 26, 1950: those domiciled in India, those who migrated from Pakistan, those who migrated to Pakistan but later returned for resettlement, and persons of Indian origin residing outside India.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the acquisition of citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955: 1️⃣ Citizenship by Birth. 2️⃣ Citizenship by Descent. 3️⃣ Citizenship by Registration. 4️⃣ Citizenship by Naturalisation.
questions.e: The Citizenship Act of 1955 prescribes five ways of acquiring citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory.

questions.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights are available only to the citizens of India and not to foreigners? 1️⃣ Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment (Article 16). 2️⃣ Protection of six rights regarding freedom of speech, assembly, etc. (Article 19). 3️⃣ Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21).
questions.e: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are Fundamental Rights available only to citizens and not to foreigners. Article 21 is available to both citizens and foreigners (except enemy aliens).

questions.q: Under Article 12 of the Constitution, the term 'State' includes: 1️⃣ Government and Parliament of India. 2️⃣ All local authorities like municipalities and panchayats. 3️⃣ Statutory authorities like LIC, ONGC, and SAIL.
questions.e: Article 12 defines 'State' broadly for the purposes of Part III to include the Union and State governments and legislatures, all local authorities, and other statutory or non-statutory authorities.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 13: 1️⃣ It provides for the doctrine of judicial review. 2️⃣ It declares that all laws inconsistent with fundamental rights shall be void. 3️⃣ The term 'law' includes permanent laws, temporary laws like ordinances, and even customs having the force of law.
questions.e: Article 13 expressively provides for judicial review by declaring inconsistent laws void. The definition of 'law' is wide, covering enacted legislation, executive orders, and non-legislative sources like custom or usage.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are correct regarding 'Equality before Law' and 'Equal Protection of Laws' under Article 14? 1️⃣ 'Equality before law' is of British origin. 2️⃣ 'Equal protection of laws' is of American origin. 3️⃣ 'Equality before law' is a positive concept, while 'Equal protection of laws' is a negative concept.
questions.e: 'Equality before law' (British) is a negative concept connoting the absence of special privileges. 'Equal protection of laws' (American) is a positive concept connoting the equality of treatment under equal circumstances.

questions.q: With reference to Article 15, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds *only* of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. 2️⃣ It prohibits discrimination only by the State and not by private individuals. 3️⃣ The State is permitted to make special provisions for women and children.
questions.e: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on specified grounds. While the first provision (15(1)) applies to the State, the second provision (15(2)) regarding access to public places prohibits discrimination by both the State and private individuals. It allows exceptions for women, children, and backward classes.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Abolition of Untouchability' under Article 17, consider the following: 1️⃣ It abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. 2️⃣ The term 'untouchability' is defined in the Constitution. 3️⃣ The right under Article 17 is available against both the State and private individuals.
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes the practice and makes its enforcement an offense. The term 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution or in any Act. The Supreme Court held that this right is available against private individuals.

questions.q: Article 18 of the Constitution: 1️⃣ Abolishes all titles including military and academic distinctions. 2️⃣ Prohibits a citizen of India from accepting any title from any foreign state. 3️⃣ Banned hereditary titles of nobility like Maharaja and Rai Bahadur.
questions.e: Article 18 abolishes titles but specifically exempts military or academic distinctions. It prohibits Indian citizens from accepting foreign titles and banned colonial-era hereditary titles as they violate the principle of equal status.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six rights guaranteed under Article 19?
o: Right to assemble peaceably and without arms.
Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
Right to form associations or unions.
Right to freedom of speech and expression.
questions.e: Originally, Article 19 contained seven rights, but the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property was deleted by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20): 1️⃣ No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once (Double Jeopardy). 2️⃣ No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself (Self-incrimination). 3️⃣ An ex-post-facto law can be enacted for civil or tax liabilities.
questions.e: Article 20 prohibits ex-post-facto criminal laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination. The limitation on ex-post-facto laws applies only to criminal laws and not to civil or tax laws, which can be imposed retrospectively.

questions.q: With reference to 'Article 21', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court in the Maneka case (1978) introduced the 'due process of law' concept. 3️⃣ It protects only against arbitrary executive action and not from arbitrary legislative action.
questions.e: In the Gopalan case (1950), the SC took a narrow view that Article 21 protects only against executive action. However, in the Maneka case (1978), it ruled that procedure must be reasonable, fair, and just, thus protecting against both arbitrary executive and legislative action.

questions.q: Article 21-A, which makes elementary education a Fundamental Right, was added to the Constitution by:
questions.e: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 added Article 21-A, providing free and compulsory education to all children aged six to fourteen years.

questions.q: Regarding 'Preventive Detention' under Article 22, consider the following: 1️⃣ It is a precautionary measure based on suspicion. 2️⃣ Detention cannot exceed three months unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause. 3️⃣ No other democratic country has made preventive detention an integral part of its Constitution as in India.
questions.e: Preventive detention is based on suspicion rather than a past offense. The Constitution limits it to three months without advisory board approval. India is unique among democratic nations for including this provision within its constitutional framework.

questions.q: Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits: 1️⃣ Traffic in human beings. 2️⃣ Begar (forced labour). 3️⃣ Compulsory service for public purposes.
questions.e: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar, and similar forms of forced labor. However, it provides an exception allowing the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes (like military service) without discrimination.

questions.q: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of:
questions.e: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous activities.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Freedom of Religion', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 25 covers both religious beliefs and religious practices. 2️⃣ Freedom of religion under Article 25 is absolute and not subject to any restrictions. 3️⃣ The right to propagate religion includes the right to convert another person.
questions.e: Article 25 covers both beliefs and rituals. However, these rights are not absolute and are subject to public order, morality, and health. The right to propagate does not include a right to convert another person, as that would impinge on others' freedom of conscience.

questions.q: Article 26 protects the 'Collective Freedom of Religion' and grants religious denominations the right to: 1️⃣ Manage its own affairs in matters of religion. 2️⃣ Own and acquire movable and immovable property. 3️⃣ Administer such property in accordance with law.
questions.e: Article 26 guarantees these specific rights to every religious denomination or its section, subject to public order, morality, and health.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Cultural and Educational Rights' (Articles 29-30) is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 29 protects the interests of minorities only. 2️⃣ Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. 3️⃣ The term 'minority' is not defined in the Constitution.
questions.e: While often assumed to be only for minorities, Article 29 uses the term 'section of citizens', which the SC held includes both minorities and majorities. Article 30 is specifically for minorities. The Constitution does not define 'minority'.

questions.q: Which Article was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as "the heart and soul of the Constitution"?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar described Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as the most important article, without which the Constitution would be a nullity.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Writ Jurisdiction', consider the following: 1️⃣ Only the Supreme Court can issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ The writ jurisdiction of the High Court is wider than that of the Supreme Court. 3️⃣ A remedy under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
questions.e: Both the SC and HCs can issue writs. The HC's jurisdiction is wider because it can issue writs for FRs and 'any other purpose', whereas the SC can only issue them for FRs. Moving the SC under Article 32 is a fundamental right, unlike the discretionary power under Article 226.

questions.q: Which writ is known as a 'bulwark of individual liberty against arbitrary detention'?
questions.e: Habeas Corpus (literally 'to have the body of') is an order issued by the court to produce a detained person and set them free if the detention is illegal.

questions.q: The 'Ninth Schedule' of the Constitution was added by which Amendment Act?
questions.e: Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule were added by the 1st Amendment Act of 1951 to protect specific laws (like land reforms) from being challenged on the grounds of violating FRs.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP)?
o: They were borrowed from the American Constitution.
They are legally enforceable by the courts.
They aim at establishing social and economic democracy.
They were described as 'Conscience of the Constitution' by Dr. Ambedkar.
questions.e: DPSPs aim to establish social and economic democracy. They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution. Granville Austin, not Dr. Ambedkar, described them and FRs as the 'Conscience of the Constitution'.

questions.q: Article 40 of the Directive Principles directs the State to:
questions.e: Article 40, a Gandhian principle, directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers to function as units of self-government.

questions.q: The 'Uniform Civil Code' for the citizens is mentioned under which Article?
questions.e: Article 44, a Liberal-Intellectual principle, directs the State to secure for all citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles was added by the 97th Amendment Act of 2011?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment added Article 43-B, directing the State to promote the voluntary formation and professional management of co-operative societies.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Prime Minister' of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He is the head of the State. 2️⃣ He is the head of the Government. 3️⃣ Article 75 says only that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President.
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the head of the Government, while the President is the head of the State. Article 75 provides a very brief mention that the PM shall be appointed by the President.

questions.q: In 1997, the Supreme Court held that a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed as Prime Minister for a period of:
questions.e: A person can be a minister (including PM) for six consecutive months without being a member of Parliament, after which they must be elected or cease to hold office.

questions.q: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of: 1️⃣ NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ National Integration Council. 3️⃣ Inter-State Council.
questions.e: The PM holds the chairmanship of these major national bodies.

questions.q: According to Article 75, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
o: The House of the People (Lok Sabha).
questions.e: Article 75(3) states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People.

questions.q: Which Cabinet Committee is often described as the "Super-Cabinet"?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is the most powerful cabinet committee, dealing with all domestic and foreign policy matters.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Cabinet Committees', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional. 2️⃣ They are set up by the Prime Minister. 3️⃣ Their membership is restricted only to Cabinet Ministers.
questions.e: Cabinet Committees are not mentioned in the Constitution. They are formed by the PM as needed. While they usually include cabinet ministers, non-cabinet ministers can also be members.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President is:
o: Optional for the President to follow.
Subject to inquiry by the Supreme Court.
questions.e: The 42nd and 44th Amendments made the council's advice binding, although the President can ask for reconsideration once. Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into the advice.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services"?
questions.e: Article 50, a Liberal-Intellectual principle, directs the state to take steps for this separation in public services.

questions.q: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' is:
o: An informal body consisting of the PM and two to four influential colleagues.
A group of ministers in charge of food security.
questions.e: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' or 'Inner Cabinet' is an informal, extra-constitutional circle of advisors where real power often resides.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle targets "equal pay for equal work for both men and women"?
questions.e: Article 39(d) directs the state to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.q: According to Article 78, who is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers?
questions.e: Article 78 explicitly lists the duty of the PM to keep the President informed about administrative affairs and decisions.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding 'Collective Responsibility': 1️⃣ Ministers sink or swim together. 2️⃣ All ministers must defend cabinet decisions in Parliament. 3️⃣ A minister who disagrees with a cabinet decision and is not prepared to defend it must resign.
questions.e: Collective responsibility requires a unified front; disagreement necessitates resignation.

questions.q: Which Act created the office of the 'Secretary of State for India'?
questions.e: The 1858 Act created the Secretary of State as a member of the British Cabinet with complete authority over Indian administration.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to:
questions.e: The Macaulay Committee was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service appointed following the Charter Act of 1853.

questions.q: Which Act introduced 'Separate Electorates' for Muslims for the first time?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced communal representation for Muslims.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was an agreement between:
questions.e: The Poona Pact retained joint electorates but provided reserved seats for the depressed classes within the Hindu fold.

questions.q: 'Viksit Bharat' targets achieved by:
questions.e: 2047 marks the centenary of independence and the target year for developed status.

questions.q: Which Article is the 'Magna Carta' of India?
questions.e: Part III is rightly described as the Magna Carta of India.

questions.q: 'Mission LiFE' was introduced to promote:
questions.e: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) nudges individuals toward mindful utilization of resources.

questions.q: Which writ is the 'bulwark of individual liberty' against arbitrary detention?
questions.e: Habeas Corpus protects against illegal detention.

questions.q: 'SASCI' loans provided to states are for a tenure of:
questions.e: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans for capital investment.

questions.q: The 'Economic Complexity Index' (ECI) rank of India in 2022:
questions.e: India's rank improved from 54 in 2012 to 42 in 2022.

questions.q: Which meeting of the GST Council introduced the revised two-rate structure?
questions.e: The 56th meeting rationalized rates into 5% and 18%.

questions.q: 'PM-JANMAN' addresses the needs of:
questions.e: It targets socio-economic development for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right protects the 'wearing and carrying of kirpans'?
questions.e: Article 25 includes an explanation that this is part of the Sikh profession.

questions.q: Which Article is called the 'soul' of the Constitution?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the very soul and heart of the Constitution.

questions.q: India leads the world in the production of:
questions.e: India holds the top global rank in milk and pulses production.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment added 'Fundamental Duties'?
questions.e: Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A) were added in 1976.

questions.q: The 'Entrepreneurial State' manages uncertainty through:
questions.e: An entrepreneurial state acts before certainty emerges and learns from course corrections.

questions.q: 'Individual Responsibility' under Article 75 means ministers hold office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: Article 75 states ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: 'NIPUN Bharat' targets foundational literacy by:
questions.e: NIPUN Bharat ensures foundational skills by the end of Grade 3.

questions.q: Which Act renamed 'United Provinces' to 'Uttar Pradesh'?
questions.e: The United Provinces was renamed in 1950.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment added a provision to Article 38 to:
o: Minimize inequalities in income and status.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment added Article 38(2).

questions.q: Under the 1919 Act, 'Dyarchy' was introduced in:
questions.e: The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy at the provincial level.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the 'Conduct of Business' of the Government?
questions.e: Article 77 specifies executive actions are in the President's name.

questions.q: 'BharatNet' project connects administrative units at:
questions.e: It connects villages with high-speed optical fiber.

questions.q: 'Sagar Mala' modernization focuses on:
questions.e: It is a port-led development program.

questions.q: The 'Account Aggregator' framework is regulated by:
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India regulates the AA ecosystem.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right guarantees 'protection of life'?
questions.e: Article 21 declares life cannot be deprived except by legal procedure.

questions.q: Which Act for the first time referred to Company's territories as 'British possessions'?
questions.e: Pitt's India Act of 1784 used this terminology.

questions.q: 'PM-KUSUM' scheme aims to:
questions.e: It targets energy security for farmers through solar power.

questions.q: Which Article abolishes 'Untouchability'?
questions.e: Article 17 forbids its practice in any form.

questions.q: 'Mission Shakti' sub-scheme 'Sambal' is for:
questions.e: Sambal is for women's safety.

questions.q: The 'Nowcasting' model integrated indicators like GST and:
questions.e: Nowcasting uses power demand for real-time growth assessment.

questions.q: 'Viksit Bharat' vision is for the year:
questions.e: 2047 marks India's centenary of independence.

questions.q: Which Article prohibits 'Forced Labor'?
questions.e: Article 23 prohibits all forms of forced labor.

questions.q: Which Act redesignated 'Governor-General of India' as 'Viceroy'?
questions.e: The 1858 Act changed the designation to Viceroy.

questions.q: India is the world's largest producer of:
questions.e: India holds top rank in milk and pulses.

questions.q: Which writ is issued to *quash* an order already passed?
questions.e: Certiorari quashes an existing order.

questions.q: 'PM-JANMAN' targets how many critical interventions?
questions.e: It addresses 11 essential services for tribal groups.

questions.q: The 'VBSA Bill' aims to grant autonomy to:
questions.e: It targets top-tier university autonomy.

questions.q: 'Account Aggregator' handles data based on:
questions.e: It is a consent-based digital system.

questions.q: Which Article describes the duties of the PM?
questions.e: Article 78 lists the PM's communication duties.

questions.q: 'Mission LiFE' nudges ______ action.
questions.e: It emphasizes individual choice power.

questions.q: Which Act introduced separate electorates?
questions.e: Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates.

questions.q: Which Article is the 'bulwark of liberty'?
questions.e: Habeas Corpus under Art 32 is a bulwark of liberty.

questions.q: Which Act created 'Secretary of State'?
questions.e: The 1858 Act created this office.

questions.q: 'PM-SVANidhi' loan is:
questions.e: It provides working capital without collateral.

questions.q: Which Article protects 'wearing of kirpans'?
questions.e: Art 25 covers this Sikh profession.

questions.q: 'SASCI' loans are for:
questions.e: Interest-free 50-year loans for states.

questions.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to form new states?
questions.e: Art 3 redraws the internal map.

questions.q: Which Article is the 'Magna Carta'?
questions.e: Part III is the Magna Carta.

questions.q: 'Critical Minerals' include:
questions.e: Lithium is vital for EV batteries.

questions.q: Who is the chairman of Inter-State Council?
questions.e: The PM chairs the Inter-State Council.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act of 1935, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They were issued to the Governors and the Governor-General by the British Government. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are essentially a modern name for these instructions. 3️⃣ The fundamental difference is that DPSPs are addressed to the legislature and the executive of the State rather than colonial administrators.
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated that the Directive Principles are like the Instrument of Instructions, which were issued to the Governor-General and to the Governors of the colonies of India by the British Government under the Government of India Act of 1935. The only difference is that they are instructions to the legislature and the executive.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Non-justiciable' nature of Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ They are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. 2️⃣ The Constitution makes them fundamental in the governance of the country. 3️⃣ The real force behind them is political, i.e., public opinion.
questions.e: The Directive Principles are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. However, Article 37 declares that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the classification of Directive Principles: 1️⃣ The Constitution formally classifies them into Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual categories. 2️⃣ Socialistic principles aim at providing social and economic justice. 3️⃣ Gandhian principles represent the programme of reconstruction enunciated by Gandhi during the national movement.
questions.e: The Constitution does not contain any classification of Directive Principles. However, on the basis of their content and direction, they are usually classified into three broad categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual.

questions.q: Which of the following Socialistic Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 38: To promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order permeated by justice. 2️⃣ Article 41: To secure the right to work, to education, and to public assistance in certain cases. 3️⃣ Article 43A: To take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries.
questions.e: These are all Socialistic principles: Article 38 focuses on social order and minimizing inequalities; Article 41 on the right to work and education; and Article 43A on workers' participation in management.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Gandhian Principles', which of the following is/are explicitly mentioned in the DPSP? 1️⃣ To organize village panchayats (Article 40). 2️⃣ To promote cottage industries in rural areas (Article 43). 3️⃣ To prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs (Article 47).
questions.e: All these are Gandhian principles: Article 40 for village panchayats, Article 43 for cottage industries, and Article 47 for the prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Liberal-Intellectual' principles: 1️⃣ Article 44: Uniform Civil Code for the citizens. 2️⃣ Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive in public services. 3️⃣ Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security.
questions.e: These fall under the Liberal-Intellectual category: Article 44 for a Uniform Civil Code, Article 50 for separating judiciary and executive, and Article 51 for international peace and security.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976? 1️⃣ Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children. 2️⃣ Article 39A: To promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor. 3️⃣ Article 43A: To secure the participation of workers in management. 4️⃣ Article 48A: To protect and improve the environment.
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles: Article 39 (opportunities for children), Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers), and Article 48A (environment protection).

questions.q: With reference to the 'Conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles', consider the following: 1️⃣ In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the SC ruled that DPSPs are subsidiary to Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ The 25th Amendment Act (1971) gave primacy to Articles 39(b) and 39(c) over Articles 14, 19, and 31. 3️⃣ In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the SC established that the balance between FRs and DPSPs is a basic feature of the Constitution.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The SC initially made DPSPs subsidiary. The 25th Amendment gave primacy to specific socialistic DPSPs. Finally, the Minerva Mills case emphasized the balance and harmony between the two as a basic feature.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made a provision for the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45, making elementary education a fundamental right (Article 21A), while the new Article 45 directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Prime Minister' of India, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ He is the real executive authority (de facto executive). 2️⃣ Article 75 says only that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President. 3️⃣ The Constitution requires that he must be a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of appointment.
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the real executive authority. Article 75 simply states he shall be appointed by the President. Statement 3 is incorrect because a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed PM for six months.

questions.q: With reference to the appointment of the Prime Minister, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When no party has a clear majority, the President may exercise personal discretion. 2️⃣ The President usually appoints the leader of the largest party or coalition as the PM. 3️⃣ The PM must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before taking the oath of office.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct regarding the President's discretionary power in a "hung Parliament". Statement 3 is incorrect; the SC has ruled the President can appoint a PM first and then ask them to prove the majority within a reasonable period.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Prime Minister’s powers in relation to the Council of Ministers: 1️⃣ He recommends persons for appointment as ministers by the President. 2️⃣ He allocates and reshuffles various portfolios among the ministers. 3️⃣ His resignation or death leads to the automatic dissolution of the council of ministers.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The PM advises the President on ministerial appointments and portfolios. Since the PM is the head, his exit collapses the entire council.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the duties of the Prime Minister as per Article 78? 1️⃣ To communicate all decisions of the council of ministers to the President. 2️⃣ To furnish information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union as the President may call for. 3️⃣ To submit for consideration of the council any matter on which a decision has been taken by a minister but not considered by the council, if the President so requires.
questions.e: All three points are explicitly listed as the PM's duties towards the President under Article 78 of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Central Council of Ministers', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 74 deals with the status of the council. 2️⃣ Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibility of ministers. 3️⃣ The council of ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 74 and 75 outline the framework for the council. Article 75 explicitly states that the council is collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President: 1️⃣ Shall be inquired into by any court. 2️⃣ Is binding on the President after the 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts. 3️⃣ The President may require the council to reconsider such advice only once.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 74(2) states that the advice shall not be inquired into by any court. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: amendments made the advice binding, though the President can ask for a one-time reconsideration.

questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Union Council of Ministers as per the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
o: 10% of the total strength of Parliament.
15% of the total strength of Parliament.
15% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
10% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Collective Responsibility' of ministers: 1️⃣ It is the fundamental principle of the parliamentary system. 2️⃣ All ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission. 3️⃣ A no-confidence motion passed against the council requires all ministers, including those from Rajya Sabha, to resign.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Collective responsibility means the council acts as a single team. If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the entire ministry must resign, regardless of which House individual ministers belong to.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Individual Responsibility' of ministers, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 75 contains the principle of individual responsibility. 2️⃣ It means that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. 3️⃣ The President can remove a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 75 states ministers hold office during the President's pleasure. In practice, this means the PM can ensure their removal by advising the President.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers in India?
o: Ministers are legally responsible for every public act of the President.
Every order of the President for a public act must be countersigned by a minister.
Courts can inquire into the legal advice given by ministers.
The Constitution of India does not provide for a system of legal responsibility of a minister.
questions.e: Unlike Britain, where ministers must countersign royal orders and are legally responsible, India has no such provision. The courts are also barred from inquiring into the advice given to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Cabinet': 1️⃣ It is a smaller body consisting of 15 to 20 ministers. 2️⃣ It was not mentioned in the original text of the Constitution. 3️⃣ It was inserted in Article 352 by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Cabinet is the inner core of the Council of Ministers. The word was added to the Constitution via the 44th Amendment to define it as the Council consisting of the PM and other Ministers of Cabinet rank.

questions.q: What is the "Super-Cabinet" according to the text?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is often described as a "Super-Cabinet" because it deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs.

questions.q: Regarding 'Cabinet Committees', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional in emergence. 2️⃣ They are of two types: standing and ad hoc. 3️⃣ They are always chaired by the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; while the PM chairs most, some are chaired by other ministers, such as the Parliamentary Affairs Committee which is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the roles of the 'Cabinet'? 1️⃣ It is the highest decision-making authority in our politico-administrative system. 2️⃣ It is the supreme direction-controlling body of the Central government. 3️⃣ it is the chief policy-formulating body of the Central government.
questions.e: The Cabinet performs all these roles as the top-tier executive and policy-formulating body of the Central government.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Kitchen Cabinet', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a formal constitutional body. 2️⃣ It consists of the PM and two to four influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It can include outsiders like family members or friends of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: The Kitchen Cabinet is an informal, extra-constitutional body. It usually consists of a few close colleagues and may sometimes include personal friends or family of the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the "Shadow Cabinet": 1️⃣ It is a unique institution of the British cabinet system. 2️⃣ It is formed by the opposition party to prepare its members for future ministerial office. 3️⃣ There is no such institution in India.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Shadow Cabinet is a British concept where opposition members "shadow" actual ministers; it does not exist in the Indian system.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles are based on 'Liberal-Intellectual' ideology? 1️⃣ To secure a uniform civil code for all citizens (Article 44). 2️⃣ To provide early childhood care and education for all children (Article 45). 3️⃣ To separate the judiciary from the executive (Article 50). 4️⃣ To promote cottage industries (Article 43).
questions.e: Articles 44, 45, and 50 are Liberal-Intellectual. Article 43 (cottage industries) is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: According to Article 39(f), the State shall direct its policy towards securing:
o: That children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner.
questions.e: Article 39(f) specifically directs the state to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Directives Outside Part IV', Article 351 deals with:
o: Claims of SCs and STs to services.
Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage.
questions.e: Article 351, located in Part XVII, directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that "Fundamental Rights are not sacrosanct and can be amended by the Parliament"?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC overruled the Golak Nath case and held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, including FRs, as long as it doesn't damage the basic structure.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the "Board of Control" is/are correct? 1️⃣ It was created by Pitt’s India Act of 1784 to manage political affairs. 2️⃣ It was empowered to supervise all operations of the civil and military government of the British possessions. 3️⃣ It was abolished by the Government of India Act of 1858.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Board of Control was established in 1784, given supervisory powers over civil/military government, and abolished in 1858 when the office of Secretary of State was created.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Regulating Act of 1773', which of the following is correct?
o: It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras independent of Bengal.
It designated the Governor of Bengal as 'Governor-General of Bengal'.
It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
It abolished the Court of Directors.
questions.e: The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal'. It made the other presidencies subordinate to Bengal.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Charter Act of 1833': 1️⃣ It was the final step towards centralisation in British India. 2️⃣ It made Lord William Bentick the first Governor-General of India. 3️⃣ It deprived the Governors of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act was the final step in centralisation, appointed Bentick as the first GG of India, and centralized legislative powers in the GG of India.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to which of the following?
questions.e: The Macaulay Committee was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service, appointed in 1854 following the Charter Act of 1853.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Government of India Act of 1858', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It changed the designation of Governor-General of India to Viceroy of India. 2️⃣ Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. 3️⃣ It created a 15-member Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.
questions.e: All statements are correct features of the 1858 Act, which established the Crown Rule.

questions.q: Which Act introduced the system of 'communal representation' for Muslims for the first time?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as Morley-Minto Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Government of India Act of 1919', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It introduced bicameralism and direct elections for the first time. 2️⃣ It divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved. 3️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a Central Public Service Commission.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act introduced bicameralism, provincial dyarchy, and led to the setup of a Public Service Commission in 1926.

questions.q: Which of the following features belong to the 'Government of India Act of 1935'? 1️⃣ Establishment of an All-India Federation. 2️⃣ Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces. 3️⃣ Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India. 4️⃣ Creation of a Federal Court.
questions.e: All these were major provisions of the lengthy 1935 Act.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was an agreement between:
o: Muslim League and the British Government.
questions.e: The Poona Pact was an agreement between the Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to retain the Hindu joint electorate while giving reserved seats to the depressed classes.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Indian Independence Act of 1947': 1️⃣ It declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947. 2️⃣ It abolished the office of Viceroy. 3️⃣ It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over Indian princely states.
questions.e: All these were key features of the 1947 Act that ended British rule.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the 'Union Constitution Committee'?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the chairman of both the Union Powers Committee and the Union Constitution Committee.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are 'Minor Committees' of the Constituent Assembly? 1️⃣ Credentials Committee. 2️⃣ House Committee. 3️⃣ Order of Business Committee. 4️⃣ Steering Committee.
questions.e: Steering Committee was a Major Committee. The others listed (Credentials, House, Order of Business) were Minor Committees.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Drafting Committee': 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members. 3️⃣ N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter who resigned due to ill-health.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The committee was chaired by Dr. Ambedkar and included members like N. Madhava Rau.

questions.q: On which date was the Constitution of India 'Adopted, Enacted and Given to themselves' by the people?
questions.e: November 26, 1949, is the date of adoption as mentioned in the Preamble.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the "Authoritative text in Hindi language"?
questions.e: Article 394A was inserted by the 58th Amendment Act of 1987 to provide for an authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

questions.q: With reference to 'Union and its Territory', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India'. 2️⃣ The 'Union of India' includes only the States. 3️⃣ The 'Territory of India' includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired.
questions.e: The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression because the 'Union of India' includes only the states.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 3 of the Constitution: 1️⃣ Parliament can form a new state by uniting a part of any state to any other state. 2️⃣ A bill for this purpose can be introduced only with the prior recommendation of the President. 3️⃣ The President must refer the bill to the state legislature for its binding opinion.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the opinion of the state legislature is not binding.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Berubari Union' case (1960), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Article 3 includes the power to diminish the area of India as a whole.
Parliament can cede Indian territory to a foreign country under Article 3.
Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368.
Settlement of boundary disputes always requires a constitutional amendment.
questions.e: The SC held that ceding Indian territory requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Evolution of States', which commission first recommended the reorganization of states on a linguistic basis?
questions.e: The Fazl Ali Commission broadly accepted language as the basis of reorganization.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of 'State - Year of Creation' is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Nagaland was formed in 1963. Gujarat (1960), Haryana (1966), and Sikkim (1975) are correctly matched.

questions.q: The 'Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill' deals with:
questions.e: It seeks to grant total autonomy to top-tier universities to reach global rankings.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act of 1935 is/are correct? 1️⃣ They were issued to the Governors and the Governor-General by the British Government. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are essentially a modern name for these instructions. 3️⃣ The fundamental difference is that DPSPs are addressed to the legislature and the executive of the State rather than colonial administrators.
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated that the Directive Principles are like the Instrument of Instructions, which were issued to the Governor-General and to the Governors of the colonies of India by the British Government under the Government of India Act of 1935. The only difference is that they are instructions to the legislature and the executive.

questions.q: With reference to the nature of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are constitutional instructions or recommendations to the State in legislative, executive, and administrative matters. 2️⃣ According to Article 36, the term 'State' in Part IV has a narrower meaning than in Part III. 3️⃣ They are intended to be the 'basis of all future legislation' in the country.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as they are recommendations to the State. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 36 explicitly states that 'State' in Part IV has the same meaning as in Part III. Statement 3 is correct as the Constituent Assembly intended them to guide all future law-making.

questions.q: According to Article 37 of the Indian Constitution, the Directive Principles are: 1️⃣ Legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. 2️⃣ Fundamental in the governance of the country. 3️⃣ The duty of the State to apply in making laws.
questions.e: Article 37 declares that the Directive Principles are non-justiciable (not legally enforceable by courts). However, it also explicitly states they are fundamental in governance and it is the State's duty to apply them in making laws.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'non-justiciable' nature of DPSPs?
o: The President can suspend them during a National Emergency.
They are subsidiary to Fundamental Rights and cannot be implemented if they conflict with any FR.
They are not legally enforceable by the courts, but their real force lies in the moral force of public opinion.
Courts can compel the government to implement them through writs.
questions.e: DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be legally enforced by courts. Their implementation depends on the moral and political force of the electorate and public opinion.

questions.q: Which of the following Socialistic Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 38: Secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people. 2️⃣ Article 41: Right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases. 3️⃣ Article 43A: Participation of workers in the management of industries.
questions.e: All three are classified as Socialistic principles aiming to provide social and economic justice. Article 38 deals with the social order, Article 41 with the right to work/education, and Article 43A with workers' participation.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Gandhian Principles' in DPSP: 1️⃣ To promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas (Article 43). 2️⃣ To promote voluntary formation and professional management of co-operative societies (Article 43B). 3️⃣ To prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs (Article 47).
questions.e: All three statements represent the Gandhian ideology in the Constitution. Statement 2 (Article 43B) was specifically added by the 97th Amendment Act of 2011.

questions.q: Under Article 39, the State is directed to secure which of the following? 1️⃣ Right to an adequate means of livelihood for all citizens. 2️⃣ Prevention of concentration of wealth and means of production. 3️⃣ Equal pay for equal work for both men and women. 4️⃣ Protection of the health and strength of workers.
questions.e: Article 39 includes all these directives as part of the Socialistic framework to ensure equitable distribution and welfare.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles was amended by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002?
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45. It now directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.q: Which of the following Liberal-Intellectual Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 44: Uniform Civil Code for the citizens. 2️⃣ Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive in the public services. 3️⃣ Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security.
questions.e: These are all classified as Liberal-Intellectual principles representing the ideology of liberalism.

questions.q: Article 39A, which provides for 'Free Legal Aid to the Poor', was added by:
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles, including Article 39A to promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles': 1️⃣ In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the SC ruled that DPSPs are subsidiary to Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ In the Golak Nath case (1967), the SC held that DPSPs cannot be implemented by taking away any of the Fundamental Rights. 3️⃣ In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the SC ruled that the balance between FRs and DPSPs is a basic feature of the Constitution.
questions.e: The history of conflict shows the SC initially making DPSPs subsidiary, then strictly protecting FRs in Golak Nath, and finally establishing the "balance" as a basic feature in Minerva Mills.

questions.q: With reference to the implementation of DPSPs, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to take up development in a planned manner. 2️⃣ The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 was enacted to safeguard forests and wildlife. 3️⃣ The Criminal Procedure Code (1973) separated the judiciary from the executive in the public services.
questions.e: All three are examples of the State implementing Directive Principles: Statement 1 relates to Articles 38 and 39, Statement 2 to Article 48A, and Statement 3 to Article 50.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, what is the maximum strength of the Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister?
o: 10% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
10% of the total strength of the Parliament.
15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
15% of the total strength of the Parliament.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 mandated that the total number of ministers, including the PM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Collective Responsibility' of the Council of Ministers is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is the fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government. 2️⃣ Article 75 explicitly states that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. 3️⃣ When the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, only the ministers from the Lok Sabha must resign.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because collective responsibility means that *all* ministers, including those from the Rajya Sabha, must resign if a no-confidence motion is passed by the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: With reference to the appointment of the Prime Minister, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution provides a specific and detailed procedure for the selection and appointment of the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ In 1980, the Delhi High Court held that a person must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before being appointed. 3️⃣ The President can exercise individual discretion when no party has a clear majority in the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as there is no specific procedure in the Constitution. Statement 2 is incorrect as the Delhi HC held that appointment can precede the majority test. Statement 3 is correct regarding the President's discretionary power in a "hung parliament".

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President: 1️⃣ Shall be inquired into in any court. 2️⃣ Is binding on the President after the 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts. 3️⃣ The President may require the Council to reconsider such advice only once.
questions.e: Article 74(2) states that advice shall *not* be inquired into in any court. The 42nd and 44th Amendments made the advice binding, with the 44th allowing the President one chance to ask for reconsideration.

questions.q: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is NOT usually chaired by the Prime Minister?
questions.e: Most cabinet committees are chaired by the PM, but the Parliamentary Affairs Committee is chaired by the Home Minister.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Kitchen Cabinet' in India: 1️⃣ It is an extra-constitutional body with no mention in the Constitution. 2️⃣ It consists of the Prime Minister and two to four influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It may include outsiders like friends and family members of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Kitchen Cabinet is an informal inner circle where real power often resides, potentially including non-ministers.

questions.q: Which of the following Prime Ministers died while in office? 1️⃣ Jawaharlal Nehru 2️⃣ Lal Bahadur Shastri 3️⃣ Indira Gandhi 4️⃣ Rajiv Gandhi
questions.e: Nehru, Shastri, and Indira Gandhi died while in office. Rajiv Gandhi was an ex-Prime Minister when he was assassinated.

questions.q: Regarding the status of 'Council of Ministers' vs 'Cabinet', consider the following: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers is a constitutional body (Article 74 and 75). 2️⃣ The word 'Cabinet' was not in the original text of the Constitution. 3️⃣ The Council of Ministers implements decisions taken by the Cabinet.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Council is broad and constitutional, 'Cabinet' was added by the 44th Amendment in 1978, and the Cabinet acts as the policy-making body for the Council.

questions.q: Which Article of the DPSP directs the State to "promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections"?
questions.e: Article 46 specifically directs the state to promote the interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections and protect them from social injustice.

questions.q: The "Political Affairs Committee" of the Cabinet is often described as a:
questions.e: This committee is often called a 'Super-Cabinet' as it deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs.

questions.q: According to Article 78, who is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers?
questions.e: Article 78 lists the PM's duty to communicate all decisions of the council of ministers relating to administration to the President.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Individual Responsibility' of ministers under Article 75?
o: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Parliament.
The Prime Minister cannot remove a minister without the President's consent.
A minister can only be removed if a no-confidence motion is passed.
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
questions.e: Article 75 contains the principle of individual responsibility, stating that ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. In practice, this means the President can remove a minister only on the advice of the PM.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added "Promotion of co-operative societies" to the DPSP?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 added Article 43B regarding co-operative societies.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers in India, consider the following: 1️⃣ There is no provision in the Constitution for the system of legal responsibility of a minister. 2️⃣ Orders of the President for public acts must be countersigned by a minister. 3️⃣ Courts are barred from inquiring into the advice given by ministers to the President.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because, unlike Britain, India does not have the system of countersignature by a minister.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services"?
questions.e: Article 50 directs the state to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister to head a 'Minority Government' in India?
questions.e: V.P. Singh (1989-1990) headed the first minority government (National Front) which depended on outside support.

questions.q: Regarding the appointment of Ministers, which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ A person can be a minister for 6 months without being a member of Parliament. 3️⃣ The salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by the President.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because salaries and allowances are determined by Parliament.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle emphasizes "Equal pay for equal work for both men and women"?
questions.e: Article 39(d) directs the state to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.q: In the context of "Parliamentary Affairs Committee", who is its chairman as per the text?
questions.e: The Parliamentary Affairs Committee is one of the important committees chaired by the Home Minister, not the PM.

questions.q: The "Shadow Cabinet" is a unique institution found in the cabinet system of:
questions.e: The Shadow Cabinet is a unique institution of the British cabinet system where the opposition party forms a parallel cabinet to track actual ministers.

questions.q: Which Article of the DPSP relates to "Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of 6 years"?
questions.e: After the 86th Amendment in 2002, Article 45 focuses on early childhood care for those under 6 years.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers is a larger body than the Cabinet. 2️⃣ The Council of Ministers meets frequently to take decisions. 3️⃣ The Cabinet is the inner core of the Council of Ministers.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Council of Ministers as a whole rarely meets; the Cabinet meets regularly for decision-making.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the "Conduct of business of the Government of India"?
questions.e: Article 77 specifies that all executive actions of the GoI shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

questions.q: "To promote international peace and security" is a Directive Principle under:
questions.e: Article 51, a Liberal-Intellectual principle, directs the state to promote international peace, security, and maintain just relations between nations.

questions.q: Under the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a minister who is disqualified on the ground of defection shall:
o: Be ineligible to be appointed as a minister again for life.
Be disqualified to be appointed as a minister until the expiry of his term or fresh election.
Only be removed from his portfolio.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment specifies that a member disqualified for defection shall also be disqualified for appointment as a minister for the remainder of his term or until re-elected.

questions.q: "Participation of workers in management of industries" is provided under:
questions.e: Article 43A, added by the 42nd Amendment, directs the state to secure workers' participation in management.

questions.q: Regarding the Prime Minister's role in the 'Council of Ministers': 1️⃣ He is the head of the Council. 2️⃣ His death dissolves the Council. 3️⃣ He can dismiss the Council without the President's advice.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; he can only advise the President to dismiss a minister or resign himself to collapse the council.

questions.q: Which DPSP directs the State to "protect and improve the environment"?
questions.e: Article 48A, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, directs the state to protect and improve the environment.

questions.q: The "Economic Affairs Committee" deals with: 1️⃣ Directing and coordinating government activities in the economic sphere. 2️⃣ Policy matters pertaining to foreign affairs. 3️⃣ Dealing with all policy matters pertaining to domestic affairs.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are handled by the Political Affairs Committee.

questions.q: Which case established the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC established that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.q: According to Article 74, there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to:
o: Appoint the Chief Justice of India.
questions.e: Article 74(1) provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Liberal-Intellectual principle?
questions.e: Article 44 is the only Liberal-Intellectual principle among the options.

questions.q: Regarding the "Appointments Committee of the Cabinet", which is correct? 1️⃣ It decides on higher level appointments in the Central Secretariat. 2️⃣ It is chaired by the Home Minister. 3️⃣ It deals with appointments to the three armed forces.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as it is chaired by the PM.

questions.q: "The state shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code" is:
questions.e: This is the explicit text of Article 44.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to become a Cabinet Minister in India?
questions.e: Raj Kumari Amrit Kaur was the Health Minister in the first cabinet of independent India in 1947.

questions.q: "Collective Responsibility" means the Council of Ministers "sink or swim together". This is related to:
questions.e: This idiom describes the principle of collective responsibility embodied in Article 75.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities"?
questions.e: Article 38(2), added by the 44th Amendment, contains this directive.

questions.q: The Prime Minister of India is:
questions.e: Under Article 75, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Board of Control' created by Pitt’s India Act of 1784? 1️⃣ It was established to manage the commercial affairs of the East India Company. 2️⃣ It was empowered to supervise all operations of the civil and military government of the British possessions. 3️⃣ It was abolished by the Government of India Act of 1858.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because commercial affairs were managed by the Court of Directors; the Board of Control managed political affairs. Statements 2 and 3 are correct regarding its supervisory powers and its abolition in 1858.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Regulating Act of 1773', consider the following: 1️⃣ It designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal'. 2️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta. 3️⃣ It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras independent of Bengal.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct features of the 1773 Act. Statement 3 is incorrect as it actually made the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q: The 'Charter Act of 1833' is significant as it: 1️⃣ Made Lord William Bentick the first Governor-General of India. 2️⃣ Deprived the Governors of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers. 3️⃣ Ended the activities of the East India Company as a commercial body.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act was the final step towards centralisation in British India.

questions.q: Which Act for the first time introduced local representation in the Indian (Central) Legislative Council?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced local representation, with 4 members appointed by the local governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal, and Agra.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Government of India Act of 1858', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ It abolished the East India Company. 2️⃣ It created the office of the Secretary of State for India. 3️⃣ It established a 15-member Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act established direct rule by the British Crown.

questions.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as:
questions.e: The 1909 Act is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, named after the Secretary of State and the Viceroy of the time.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1919: 1️⃣ It introduced dyarchy at the provincial level. 2️⃣ It provided for a bicameral legislature at the Centre for the first time. 3️⃣ It separated provincial budgets from the Central budget.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act, also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, brought major structural changes.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was an agreement between the Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to:
o: Retain the Hindu joint electorate and give reserved seats to the depressed classes.
Form a coalition government with the Muslim League.
Accept the Communal Award in its original form.
questions.e: The Poona Pact modified the Communal Award by dropping separate electorates for depressed classes in favor of reserved seats within the joint electorate.

questions.q: Which of the following features belong to the Government of India Act of 1935? 1️⃣ Establishment of an All-India Federation. 2️⃣ Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces. 3️⃣ Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India. 4️⃣ Creation of a Federal Court.
questions.e: All these were key provisions of the lengthy and detailed 1935 Act.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947: 1️⃣ Ended the British rule and declared India an independent state. 2️⃣ Abolished the office of Viceroy. 3️⃣ Granted freedom to princely states to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
questions.e: All statements correctly describe the provisions of the Independence Act.

questions.q: Who was the chairman of the 'Union Powers Committee' of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the chairman of the Union Powers Committee, Union Constitution Committee, and the States Committee.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Drafting Committee': 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members. 3️⃣ Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman. 4️⃣ It took more than a year to prepare the first draft.
questions.e: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect as the committee took less than six months (sitting for 141 days) to prepare the draft.

questions.q: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force (commencement date)?
questions.e: While some provisions came into force on Nov 26, 1949, the major part of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950.

questions.q: Which Article was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as 'an Article without which this Constitution would be a nullity'?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar described Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as the most important article, the soul and heart of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to Article 14, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ 'Equality before law' is of British origin. 2️⃣ 'Equal protection of laws' is of American origin. 3️⃣ Equality before law is a negative concept.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 14 includes both these concepts to establish legal equality.

questions.q: Article 15(2) prohibits discrimination against citizens regarding access to shops, restaurants, and public resorts by:
o: Neither, it is a non-binding directive.
Both the State and private individuals.
questions.e: Article 15(2) explicitly prohibits discrimination by both the State and private persons regarding the use of public places.

questions.q: The 103rd Amendment Act (2019) added provisions to Article 15 and 16 for:
o: Reservation for women in the Parliament.
Reservation for SCs and STs in private institutions.
Reservation of up to 10% for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
questions.e: The 103rd Amendment enabled reservation for EWS in both educational admissions and public employment.

questions.q: Which Article abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice?
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its enforcement an offense punishable by law.

questions.q: Under Article 19, which of the following was deleted as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978?
o: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
questions.e: Originally there were seven rights in Article 19, but the property right was removed.

questions.q: Protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20) includes: 1️⃣ No ex-post-facto law. 2️⃣ No double jeopardy. 3️⃣ No self-incrimination.
questions.e: Article 20 provides these three specific protections for an accused person.

questions.q: The Supreme Court in the Maneka case (1978) introduced which concept into Article 21?
questions.e: The Maneka case introduced the 'due process' concept, requiring legal procedures to be reasonable, fair, and just.

questions.q: Article 21-A, providing free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14, was added by:
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 made elementary education a Fundamental Right.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Writs', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ Only the Supreme Court can issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ The writ jurisdiction of the High Court is wider than that of the Supreme Court. 3️⃣ Habeas Corpus literally means 'to have the body of'.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as High Courts also issue writs under Article 226. Statement 2 is correct because HCs can issue writs for FRs and 'any other purpose'. Statement 3 is correct.

questions.q: Which writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court to *quash* an order already passed?
questions.e: Certiorari is issued to quash an order based on excess or lack of jurisdiction.

questions.q: Article 33 empowers the ______ to restrict Fundamental Rights of the armed forces.
questions.e: Article 33 gives this exclusive power to the Parliament to ensure discipline in the forces.

questions.q: 'Martial Law' in India is:
o: Can only be declared by the Supreme Court.
questions.e: Martial Law is not defined but is implicit in Article 34. It differs from National Emergency as it suspends ordinary courts/government.

questions.q: The 'Ninth Schedule' was added to the Constitution to protect laws from judicial review by:
questions.e: Added in 1951, it protects laws (like land reforms) from being challenged on FR grounds.

questions.q: Which case established that 'Judicial Review' is a basic feature of the Constitution?
questions.e: The Minerva Mills case (1980) struck down provisions that sought to exclude judicial review, holding it as a basic feature.

questions.q: The Directive Principles are described as the 'Conscience of the Constitution' by:
questions.e: Granville Austin used this term for the Fundamental Rights and DPSPs together.

questions.q: Article 44 directs the State to secure for all citizens:
questions.e: Article 44 is a Liberal-Intellectual principle for a Uniform Civil Code.

questions.q: Regarding the appointment of the Prime Minister, Article 75 states:
o: The PM is selected by the Lok Sabha.
The PM is chosen by the Chief Justice.
The PM is appointed by the President.
The PM must be a member of Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: Article 75(1) states simply that the PM shall be appointed by the President.

questions.q: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of: 1️⃣ NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ National Integration Council. 3️⃣ Inter-State Council.
questions.e: The PM chairs all these major national bodies.

questions.q: According to Article 75, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
o: The House of the People (Lok Sabha).
questions.e: Collective responsibility is specifically to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' is an:
questions.e: It is a small circle of advisors to the PM, not mentioned in the Constitution.

questions.q: Which Cabinet Committee is often called the 'Super-Cabinet'?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is the most powerful cabinet committee.

questions.q: 'Individual Responsibility' under Article 75 means ministers hold office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: While appointed on PM's advice, they constitutionally hold office during the President's pleasure.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to 'separate the judiciary from the executive'?
questions.e: This is a Liberal-Intellectual directive in Article 50.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister to head a 'Minority Government' in India?
questions.e: V.P. Singh (1989-90) led the first minority government (National Front).

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) resulted in:
o: Reserved seats for depressed classes within joint electorates.
questions.e: It was an agreement between Congress and Dr. Ambedkar.

questions.q: Which Act created the office of the 'Secretary of State for India'?
questions.e: This act established the office as a member of the British Cabinet.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to:
questions.e: It was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service.

questions.q: Which Act introduced 'Communal Representation' for Muslims?
questions.e: The Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates.

questions.q: Under the 1919 Act, 'Dyarchy' was introduced in:
questions.e: The 1919 Act brought dyarchy (dual rule) to provinces.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the 'Conduct of Business' of the Indian Government?
questions.e: Article 77 specifies that executive actions are taken in the President's name.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment Act added a provision to Article 38 to:
o: Minimize inequalities in income and status.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) added Article 38(2).

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right guarantees 'Equality of opportunity in public employment'?
questions.e: Article 16 provides this guarantee to all citizens.

questions.q: India leads the world in the production of:
questions.e: India holds top global rank in milk and pulses.

questions.q: 'Viksit Bharat' targets India becoming developed by:
questions.e: 2047 is the centenary of independence.

questions.q: The 'Critical Minerals Mission' is vital for:
questions.e: Lithium and Cobalt are essential for EV batteries.

questions.q: Which writ is the 'bulwark of individual liberty'?
questions.e: It protects against arbitrary detention.
